content:
Apple turns 50 this year, and some of its customers are even more seasoned than that. Apple has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, primarily through accessibility settings.

From adjusting the font size on your Apple Watch to setting your iPhone to alert you when the washing machine finishes a cycle, the list covers a wide range of tips...

Apple says its goal is to make technology accessible to everyone, including older users.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone, including older users. That's why our products and services are designed with different needs in mind, featuring built-in accessibility functions that let you connect, create, and pursue what you love in the way that suits you best. As life evolves, so does the way we engage with the world. From enlarging on-screen text to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to flexibly adapt to your needs.

The support page primarily lists accessibility features, organised into ten categories.

  • Vision: View screen content more easily
  • Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Adjust how you control and navigate your devices
  • Speech: Speak in your own way
  • Cognitive: Focus and stay in control with ease
  • Personalisation: Create an experience that's uniquely yours
  • Organisation: Keep track of what matters
  • Health: Stay informed about your wellbeing with practical information
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay in touch

Take the Vision category as an example — it includes options like enlarging text, switching to bold fonts, inverting colours, setting colour filters, reducing transparency, boosting contrast, and minimising on-screen movement. Some features, such as Sound Recognition, were heavily promoted by Apple when they first launched but remain unfamiliar to many users.

Sound Recognition detects specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when they're detected. The feature can recognise 15 different sounds — and you can train your device to recognise your own name, as well as distinctive electronic sounds in your environment, such as the beeps from kitchen appliances, specific types of alarm systems, or doorbells. For HomePod, Sound Recognition can also pick up smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay — your iPhone will detect sirens, horns, and even a baby crying. When using CarPlay, you'll receive an on-screen notification in your car when a specific sound is detected.

This page is genuinely impressive, giving a clear picture of just how many accessibility features Apple's devices now offer. Each section provides dedicated guidance for individual supported devices. Depending on the feature, coverage may include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.
